commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
Use the PJRT wheel built with NCCL 2.30.7 headers (#9062)

Bump the ARM64 GPU PJRT wheel from XLA `3a8f3392723e` to
[`b040736f2c4a`](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/releases/tag/marin-xla-pjrt-20260909-b040736f2c4a),
adopting the NCCL 2.30.7 build-header default from
[marin-community/xla#22](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/pull/22).
This aligns compiled NCCL headers with the 2.30.7 runtime in Marin's GPU
training lock. JAX stays at 0.11.1, and all other data in `uv.lock` is
unchanged.

The release passed ragged all-to-all correctness checks on two GB200
GPUs with NCCL runtime 2.31.2, including confirmation that XLA's ragged
all-to-all device kernel executed. Marin's four-GB200 ragged-EP gate
also passed with the locked NCCL 2.30.7 runtime, checking forward
outputs, gradients, and dropped assignments against a dense reference
across four seeds.

At hero scale on 2026-09-09 (11 racks, 704 GPUs, restoring
`step-81716`), the `3a8f3392723e` wheel hung four of four attempts on
one rack's expert-parallel domain (rack indices 7, 9, 1, 2 after 43, 0,
0, 0 steps), with the #8870 signature: one rack at half CPU, every
cross-rack AllReduce one member exactly three operations behind. A
pre-merge build of this change (`b183c591142c`, the same source) then
ran 225 clean steps including a 5.4 TB checkpoint, tracking the
pooled-wave control step for step at −0.0064 nats with drops 1e-4 vs
3.4e-2 and MFU 23.3% vs 21.5%. Evidence is on
marin-community/marin#8506; the mechanism is the 2.29.7 compat shim's
per-rack LSA cliques without bounded barriers.

`trigger_hero.sh` relaunches the hero as
`hero-ragged_a2a-nccl2307-ep-step81k` from the same `step-81716`
handoff, so the first 200 steps replay the validated window against the
control and the lineage stays on main commits.

Part of #8870.

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Fix two dataset loaders and drop the no-op prepare_workdir hook (#9040)

`AudioTextUrlDataSource.resolve_audio_pointer` handles the three
HuggingFace
Audio encodings. Its `_load_audio_file` helper took a `file_name`
argument but
opened the enclosing `audio_pointer` instead, so the `{"path": ...}`
encoding
handed a dict to `open_url` and raised `AttributeError: 'dict' object
has no
attribute 'startswith'` inside rigging's filesystem guard. The
bare-string
encoding worked because the two values coincide there. The helper now
opens its
argument.

`load_datasets` in `marin/transform/huggingface/dataset_to_eval.py`
builds one
dataset per (subset, split) pair, then required `len(datasets) ==
len(subsets)`. Any config naming more than one split raised "Not all
subsets
succeeded" even when every pair loaded, so the two- and three-split
configs in
`experiments/datasets/eval.py` could not be converted. The check now
records the
pairs whose `load_dataset` call raised and names them in the error, and
rejects
an empty `splits` list, which converts nothing. Single-split configs
behave as
before.

`ContainerRuntime.prepare_workdir` has been empty in both
`DockerRuntime` and
`ProcessRuntime` since #3696 moved task workdirs onto the already-tmpfs
`cache_dir`. The protocol still described it as "Docker: mounts a
per-task tmpfs
for quota enforcement" and `TaskAttempt._setup` read
`resources.disk_bytes` only
to pass it in, under a comment claiming staged files had to land on that
tmpfs.
No quota is enforced. Remove the protocol method, both empty
implementations,
the call site, and a test that asserted nothing.

Each loader fix carries a regression test that fails against the
previous code.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nightshift Agent <nightshift@marin.local>

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Split Ruff import configuration by package (#9028)

Run root and Marin package files under separate Ruff configurations. The
root
configuration keeps `experiments` local and groups Marin imports
consistently;
`lib/marin/pyproject.toml` extends the root rules while treating Marin
as
first-party.

`infra/pre-commit.py` excludes `lib/marin` from the generic Python pass
and
invokes its package configuration separately. This prevents Ruff from
moving
individual Marin imports across the `experiments` boundary. The affected
source
changes are import-only reorganizations.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[loom] Lower Marina session reasoning effort (#9064)

Run new sessions launched through Marina's embedded agent panel at low
reasoning effort. This favors response latency for bounded, read-only
page questions.

Existing sessions retain the effort recorded in their launch snapshot.
The production Loom deployment must be applied after merge for new
sessions to inherit the setting.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Add the embedded agent panel (#9055)

Add a shared Ask Marina panel for checked-in applications. An opted-in
app selects its Loom profile, repository, and starter questions in
`app.toml`, then publishes a versioned page context of at most 16 KiB.
The panel launches an ACP session in one request, streams its transcript
and tool activity, and restores the same conversation after refresh.

Loom remains the durable session store. The browser keeps only a
20-entry mapping from the signed-in Loom user, Loom origin, app, and
page context to a Loom session ID; drafts remain in session storage.
Changing users, Loom origins, or page contexts rebinds the panel to the
corresponding session.

Generate a read-only FastMCP projection from the same registered OpenAPI
operations as the full Marina MCP endpoint. The deployed `marina`
profile receives only this MCP group. The full group remains available
for separately configured workflows.

Plantt is the first integration. It supplies the chart ID, revision,
selection, and save/conflict state without sending the chart document.
Its scripted Loom journey covers launch inputs, paged transcript
history, live tool activity, the final answer, page-context changes,
phone/tablet/desktop layouts, and restoration without a duplicate launch
or prompt.

Use the exact-origin credentialed browser API added in
marin-community/loom#350.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Return the EP hero to the ragged all-to-all transport (#9043)

Restore `ragged_all_to_all` as the hero's MoE backend with fp32 weights
on device, reverting the pooled-wave fallback from #8884. The
diagnostics, soak, and benchmarks follow the hero.

The fallback was taken after two ragged hero attempts hung silently on
one rack at 11 racks (#8870). Since then, one train-step executable per
rank removed the duplicate symmetric-window registration (#8911), the
PJRT wheel moved to the balanced ragged device kernel with 128-thread
CTAs (#8976), and QuACK 0.6.4 replaces the grouped-GEMM scheduler that
left outputs unwritten under contention (#8959, merge first). The hang's
root cause is still open. The strongest lead is a fabric fault on
specific NVL72 domains, which the 2026-09-05 NVLink fault on the
pooled-wave hero also fits. The redeployment is a 200-step trial against
the pooled-wave run on the same batches, with rollback to the
pooled-wave commit.

The live hero's checkpoints carry a pinned-host fp32 master, which
restores into device mode in process. The reverse migration is refused,
so a rollback resumes the pooled-wave run's own tree.

`trigger_hero.sh` launches `hero-ragged_a2a-ep-step81k` from the
checkpoint forced on `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k` at step 81716
(3.77T tokens on the pooled-wave transport); its metadata is marked
non-temporary so the old run's hourly save keeps it while the old run
trains the 200-step control window.

Part of #8870.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
Upgrade QuACK to 0.6.4 to fix GEMM scheduling corruption (#8959)

Upgrade QuACK from 0.6.1 to 0.6.4 to include the [Cluster Launch Control
scheduling
fix](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/quack/commit/58cb592a1a6ef85a69e37d0b4eb50217b59d20ca).
The old scheduler can leave grouped matrix-multiplication outputs
unwritten under GPU contention; [GB200 experiments reproduced this
corruption](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8870#issuecomment-5548861875).
Its connection to the training hangs in #8870 remains unproved.

QuACK 0.6.4 requires CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2 and changes the gated epilogue
API and batch-axis convention. Adapt the JAX launchers to those APIs
while preserving public tensor shapes, physical storage, tile geometry,
and CLC settings.

Lint and type checks passed, along with 1,529 safe tests and 28 selected
GB200 kernel and attention cases. The full-rack validation is the ragged
all-to-all hero redeployment's 200-step trial window, which compares the
new run against the pooled-wave control on the same batches; MFU and
loss-trajectory effects are unmeasured before it. Review material loss
differences as possible consequences of control corruption, rather than
automatically rejecting the upgrade.

Part of #8870.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Preserve XLA cross-entropy tiles and TPU accuracy (#8960)

Keep the requested XLA cross-entropy batch tile when the row count is
irregular. Pad forward and backward batch tiles independently, then
slice the outputs so dummy rows receive zero cotangents. Each pass adds
fewer rows than its tile size, including when the two tile sizes are
relatively prime. For 8519 rows, a requested 256-row batch tile
previously shrank to seven rows (the largest divisor of 8519 no greater
than 256) and required 1217 GEMMs per vocabulary pass; padding uses 34
tiles.

Request JAX's HIGHEST accuracy for TPU exponentials and logarithms in
forward logsumexp and backward softmax probabilities. The [TPU accuracy
investigation](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/373) traced roughly 1e-4
absolute differences in per-row loss and logsumexp between
vocabulary-blocked and full-vocabulary evaluation to default TPU
logarithms, including a divisible-row control. Select the accurate math
at compilation so CPU and GPU retain their existing math.

The [H100 investigation](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/362) measured
isolated forward-plus-backward time dropping from 6.357 to 0.241
seconds, with before/after loss, logsumexp, input gradients, and weight
gradients matching at unchanged 1e-5 absolute-plus-relative tolerances.
For packed Snowball 67B on 32 H100s with PP4/EP8, 34 microbatches, and
capacity factor 16 held fixed, the whole-model benchmark improved from
402.712 to 83.247 seconds per warm scoring-and-update iteration.
Whole-model numerical parity remains unresolved; the timing result does
not establish it.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Drain FA4 copies before reusing padding-tile storage (#8961)

Make FA4/CuTe attention return stable zero outputs for entirely padded
query tiles. These tiles skip the key loop that normally waits for
asynchronous query and key copies, allowing a pending query copy to
overwrite output in shared storage. Drain the copies and synchronize the
thread block before the output epilogue reuses that storage.

The 8520-token BF16 regression failed for both causal and sliding-window
attention before the fix and passed afterward on H100. It checks exact
repeated outputs, zero padding outputs and gradients, and valid outputs
and gradients against dense attention over the 40 valid prefix tokens.
The before/after evidence is recorded in [the incident
report](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/358).

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[loom] Register Marina's remote MCP server (#8971)

Register Marina’s authenticated Streamable HTTP endpoint as a remote MCP
server in Loom’s deployment config, and add an interactive marina
profile that selects the marina group. The ACP provider discovers
find_tool and call_tool from FastMCP through tools/list, so the
deployment does not duplicate the server’s inventory. The declaration
explicitly selects IAP authentication with the public OAuth audience. At
ACP process start, Loom mints a short-lived IAP token from its VM
service account and places it in the remote server’s authorization
header. The deployment manifest stores no bearer token.

Existing profile declarations list named built-in MCP groups instead of
using mcpAccess: all. Explicit selection keeps later remote
registrations out of GitHub, Slack, ferry, review, code-health, and ops
sessions unless the corresponding profile adds their group.

The marina profile tells the model to treat page and API content as
untrusted data and to call mutating operations only when the user
explicitly requests them. This is guidance, not API authorization. ACP
does not expose a header-refresh callback. Loom remints the token when
the ACP process starts or recovers, so a continuously active process may
need recovery after token expiry.

This configuration requires the remote-MCP deployment contract, native
ACP HTTP descriptors, and explicit IAP authentication added by
marin-community/loom#348, plus protocol-native tool discovery from
marin-community/loom#349. Older Loom binaries reject the manifest.

commits.author: ethantsliu
commits.message:
[eval] Load GSM8K from openai/gsm8k (#8979)

Use `openai/gsm8k` as the default `dataset_path` for Levanter's built-in
`gsm8k` and `gsm8k_cot` task specs. Caller-supplied `dataset_path`
values still pass through unchanged.

When `dataset_path` is unset, Levanter's pinned lm-eval task definitions
default to the bare `gsm8k` identifier. With `datasets==4.8.5` and
`huggingface-hub==1.21.0`, dataset loading rejects that identifier
before evaluation begins.

Fixes #7004

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[marina] Add shared Plantt planning charts (#8980)

Add Plantt as a checked-in Marina application at `/plantt/`. Charts live
in
the app-owned Postgres schema and use stable UUID routes. Optimistic
revisions
prevent stale edits from overwriting newer saves, and compressed Plantt
links
remain supported as an import path.

The Vue interface renders workstreams, tasks, dependencies, milestones,
annotations, and accelerator-capacity lanes. It supports autosave, short
share
links, JSON import and export, library filtering, and explicit conflict
recovery. The production bundle is 137.6 kB (50.6 kB gzip).
